newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia Metals--Japan aluminium premiums remain firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals--Japan aluminium premiums remain firm.

text.p: Japan's aluminium premiums were flat to slightly firmer over the past week, buoyed by strength in the U.S. market, although activity in Japan's physical metal markets was generally subdued, traders said on Wednesday.

Aluminium premiums for supply contracts for the April-June quarter were set last week at $82 to $83 a tonne over cash London Metal Exchange prices and were said to be hovering near the mid-$80s this week.
Several traders said they believed premiums were peaking, however, with one doubting the U.S. Midwest premium would be able to make a sustained rise above six cents a lb.
Premiums for Japanese end-users, who continued to buy largely on a hand-to-mouth basis, remained up to $10 a tonne below those paid by importers.
The zinc market continued to be very tight, traders said, reflecting strong demand from automobile manufacturers and other sectors.

Japanese zinc refiner Toho Zinc Co said on Wednesday it planned a modest increase in production in the fiscal year beginning in April to 125,000 tonnes from an expected 120,000 tonnes in 1996/97. The move will not involve a rise in production capacity.
Earlier this year, Dowa Mining Co said it planned to boost capacity at its majority-owned Iijima smelter by 20,000 tonnes per year, also in response to strong demand.

Traders expected Japan's domestic demand for automobiles to wane after April's increase in the national sales tax to five percent from three percent, although export demand remained brisk due to the weak yen.

Copper demand was termed dull, however, with the spot market virtually at a standstill as domestic smelter output and imports through long-term contracts proved sufficient to meet end-users' needs, traders said.

Additional agreements were reached over the past week between Australian mining companies and Japanese smelters on zinc treatment charges, adhering largely to the benchmark of $170 a tonne at an LME base price of $1,000 a tonne.

Taking into account specific penalties and other details of individual contracts, one source said the Japanese were securing about the same terms as those agreed to in early February by Canadian miner Cominco and European smelter Metaleurop.
